pending_qa.q: How does having sales targets and KPIs impact sales behavior and accountability?
pending_qa.r: Metrics, targets, and KPIs are essential because you cannot manage what you do not measure. They help you understand whether you are doing the right things and driving revenue. Clear targets allow organizations to set salespeople up for success by giving them a clear guide as to what their responsibility is, whether that is new business or account management.

pending_qa.q: What is the typical conversion rate in IT sales and how should sales teams establish realistic goals?
pending_qa.r: In IT sales, conversion rates typically sit between 30 to 50 percent for every ten prospects. To set realistic goals, you need to understand the business you are in and start collecting data on how you have performed previously, as well as knowing what the norms are in the marketplace. Without understanding your current baseline, it is hard to set goals and targets for the future.

pending_qa.q: How should salespeople adapt their communication style to different personality types?
pending_qa.r: Sales is fundamentally about psychology and understanding people. The key is to become a chameleon without losing your authenticity. For example, if you are results-driven and aggressive but selling to someone who is analytical or relationship-focused, you must adapt your presentation style, communication, and follow-ups to their personality. Understanding whether someone wants highlights or detailed information allows you to tailor your approach for greater influence.

pending_qa.q: What is the importance of addressing root causes rather than surface-level challenges in sales?
pending_qa.r: Deeply rooted challenges are normally what is most compelling in a sale, whereas surface-level issues are never the actual problem. When you start unpicking the layers and asking deeper questions, you discover the real challenges that drive decision-making. This requires becoming an expert in the customer's industry so you can provide genuine value and build rapport beyond just pitching solutions.

pending_qa.q: How long does it typically take to close a deal and why is consistent follow-up critical?
pending_qa.r: Only 2% of sales happen in the first or second contact, with most occurring between the fifth and twelfth contact. However, most salespeople do not follow up, which is why persistence and value-driven engagement at each touchpoint are essential. A deal can take over three years to close if the customer has existing commitments or long buying cycles, as in the MSP and IT provider industry.

pending_qa.q: Why is mentoring and coaching important even for experienced or top-performing salespeople?
pending_qa.r: No matter where you are in your sales journey, you are always going to need support, mentoring, coaching, and feedback. Even the best sports people in the world at Olympic level still have coaches, sometimes multiple coaches, to further improve and identify blind spots. Difficult, honest feedback is more valuable than praise because it shows where you can improve, and continuous improvement is essential in sales.

pending_qa.q: How should salespeople determine which activities drive the most success?
pending_qa.r: You need to go back and understand where success is coming from and how you can spend more time doing those activities. For example, at Pax8 Academy, they know they drive much more engagement and opportunity when they are at events and having those conversations. Understanding your specific role and industry is crucial, as the activities that drive results will vary by position and sector.

pending_qa.q: What is the relationship between reliability in small tasks and delivery on major commitments in sales?
pending_qa.r: Responsiveness and doing what you say you will do are essential indicators of a good salesperson. If you cannot do the little things reliably, you will never deliver on the big things. Building trust through small actions creates the foundation for larger deals and lasting client relationships.
